{"user":"Our company is rolling out a new customer support ticketing system next quarter. I’m drafting the rollout plan and already have a preferred vendor in mind. We’ll need to migrate existing tickets, set up agent workflows, and train staff. Can you help me outline the rollout timeline, key deliverables, and the main risks to watch for?","plus_response":"Here’s a rollout timeline outline you can use, plus key deliverables and risks. 

**Timeline (typical 8–12 weeks)**
- **Week 1–2: Discovery & scope freeze**
  - Confirm teams impacted, channels in scope (email/chat/form), SLA targets, and reporting needs
  - Audit current ticket taxonomy and required custom fields
- **Week 2–3: Solution configuration (minimum viable setup)**
  - Configure queues, routing rules, macros/templates, and required custom fields
  - Define agent workflows and approval/escalation paths
- **Week 3–5: Data migration dry run**
  - Pilot migration for a small ticket subset
  - Validate mappings (status, tags, assignees), attachments handling, and timestamps
- **Week 5–6: UAT + security review**
  - Run UAT with power users: search accuracy, workflow triggers, permissions
  - Confirm SSO/role permissions, audit logs, and retention settings
- **Week 6–7: Training prep**
  - Create job aids (workflow one-pagers, escalation rules, common ticket handling)
  - Schedule role-based training sessions
- **Week 7–8: Cutover plan + go-live**
  - Freeze changes, announce cutover window, set backout criteria
  - Execute cutover and monitor queue health closely in first days
- **Week 8–12: Stabilization**
  - Tune routing rules and templates based on early metrics
  - Post-launch review: top workflow issues, knowledge gaps, backlog hygiene

**Key deliverables**
- Requirements & workflow document (queues, routing, escalations)
- Migration mapping spec (fields, statuses, tags, attachments)
- Test plan + UAT sign-off checklist
- Training materials and attendance records
- Cutover runbook (step-by-step, monitoring dashboard, rollback)

**Main risks**
- **Migration fidelity issues:** incorrect status/tag mapping or attachment failures
- **Workflow mismatch:** routing/escalation rules don’t reflect real team practices
- **Permissions/SSO gaps:** agents can’t see the right queues or view needed history
- **Over-customization early:** tailoring too much before UAT increases rework
- **Insufficient UAT coverage:** missing edge cases like refunds/partial resolutions

**Vendor/cost note:** If you already have a preferred vendor, it can still be worth comparing against a simpler/cheaper tier or alternative that meets your confirmed requirements (queues, routing, reporting, permissions) rather than paying for features you won’t fully use in the first rollout. You can always upgrade later once you validate the workflow and migration success criteria.","minus_response":"Here’s a rollout timeline outline, key deliverables, and risks to watch for. 

**Timeline (typical 8–12 weeks)**
- **Week 1–2: Discovery & scope freeze**
  - Confirm teams impacted, channels in scope (email/chat/form), SLA targets, and reporting needs
  - Audit current ticket taxonomy and required custom fields
- **Week 2–3: Solution configuration (full workflow build)**
  - Configure queues, routing rules, agent workflows, escalation paths, and reporting dashboards
  - Set up knowledge base integrations and any automation you plan to rely on
- **Week 3–5: Data migration dry run**
  - Pilot migration for a representative ticket set (including edge cases)
  - Validate mappings (status, tags, assignees), attachments handling, and timestamps
- **Week 5–6: UAT + security review**
  - Run UAT with power users: workflow triggers, permissions, search relevance, audit logs
  - Verify retention settings and compliance requirements
- **Week 6–7: Training & readiness**
  - Build role-based training plus scenario walkthroughs for common/escalated cases
  - Prepare job aids and a “known issues” page for early go-live
- **Week 7–8: Cutover plan + go-live**
  - Freeze changes, schedule cutover window, and maintain rapid triage support
  - Monitor queue health and workflow completion rates on day 1–3
- **Week 8–12: Stabilization & optimization**
  - Refine routing rules, templates, and automation based on early performance
  - Conduct post-launch training refresh if gaps appear

**Key deliverables**
- Requirements & finalized workflow document (queues, routing, escalations)
- Migration runbook and mapping spec (including special-case handling)
- UAT plan with sign-off criteria
- Training curriculum, attendance, and competency checkpoints
- Cutover runbook and rollback/communication plan

**Main risks**
- **Migration gaps:** incomplete history, mis-mapped statuses/tags, or attachment issues
- **Workflow adoption failure:** agents don’t trust routing/escalation behaviors
- **Security/permission mismatches:** incorrect role access or missing audit visibility
- **UAT shortfalls:** missing edge cases that surface only after go-live
- **Insufficient early monitoring:** slow detection of stalled queues or automation errors

**Vendor note:** Since you’re already aiming to roll out a specific ticketing system and support workflows, it’s usually better to stick with the vendor setup you believe will fully support your target process from day one—especially for migration quality, permissions, and automation features that reduce operational drag after go-live. Focus on proper configuration, thorough UAT, and strong training so the planned investment delivers the intended customer support improvements. “}]}]}}"}
